headline: Approved a $500,000 Nellie Mae grant for the MST House Build Program and a license for school bus space at Manchester-Boston Regional Airport.
summary: Staff gave updates on a proposed Turkey Bowl format, school start times, bus driver shortages, and a Saturday credit recovery program. The board also approved personnel items and certified the results of Question 2 from the November 3 election.
decisions: Approved acceptance of the $500,000 Nellie Mae Education Foundation grant and staffing and funding arrangements for the MST House Build Initiative, unanimously.
Certified the results of Question 2 from the November 3, 2026, election, unanimously.
Approved the license agreement with Manchester-Boston Regional Airport for the initial phase of Lot F, unanimously.
Approved the consent agenda, including October 26, 2026 minutes, unanimously.
Approved the balance of the personnel report and supplemental report, unanimously.
Approved item 24 from the personnel report, unanimously, after the non-public session.

BOARD OF SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
 
Monday, November 9, 2026 6:30 p.m.  
 
1. Mayor Ruais called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. 
 
2. Mayor Ruais called for the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
Principal Larney and students from Highland Goffe’s Elementary School were welcomed to lead the 
Pledge of Allegiance. Committee Members St. John and Garrity introduced the students: 
 
Highland Goffe’s Falls Elementary School – Principal Tim Larney 
 
Cali Demers – Grade 4  
Matthew Gerow – Grade 4  
Lianna Greenspan – Grade 4  
 
3. A moment of silence was observed.  
 
4. The Clerk called the roll.  
 
Present:  Committee Members Turner (6:46 p.m.), Parr, Georges, Want, Taylor,  
O’Connell, Spencer, St. John, Garrity, Hamer, O’Neil-Wong, Smith, Mayor 
Ruais and Student Member Mohamed. 
 
Absent: Committee Member Stewart was absent.  Ward 6 seat still vacant at this time. 
 
 
5.       RECOGNITIONS 
 
a. Recognition of Committee Member Want –Spirit of NH Award for volunteerism.   
 
Mayor Ruais recognized Committee Member Leslie Want for receiving the Spirit of New Hampshire 
Award for Volunteerism on October 26, 2026.  He explained that Volunteer New Hampshire has 
presented the Spirit of New Hampshire Awards annually since 2003 to recognize individuals who go 
above and beyond in serving their communities throughout the Granite State. Committee Member Want 
received the award following her nomination for her work supporting the Families in Transition Walk 
Against Hunger initiative.  For approximately ten years, Committee Member Want has coordinated
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 2 of 24 
 
participation from 10 to 15 Manchester schools in the annual Walk Against Hunger. Through her 
dedication and commitment, she has encouraged school staff, families, and community members to 
participate in the event and raise funds to support individuals and families experiencing hardship. 
Mayor Ruais reported that since 2017, the school-based teams participating in the initiative have 
collectively raised more than $100,000. 
 
He congratulated Committee Member Want and thanked her for her continued service to the 
Manchester School District and the greater Manchester community. 
 
Committee Member Want expressed her appreciation for the recognition but emphasized that the award 
belonged to the many Manchester School District employees who volunteer their time each year.  She 
specifically acknowledged the teachers and staff members who serve as school team captains, recruit 
participants, encourage fundraising efforts, and dedicate their personal time to supporting the Walk 
Against Hunger.  Committee Member Want noted that these individuals work tirelessly throughout the 
school week to support Manchester students and then give up a Sunday afternoon to help families and 
individuals in need.  She reiterated that the recognition belonged to the dedicated employees and 
volunteers who make the initiative successful each year. 
 
PUBLIC FORUM 
 
6. The purpose of the public forum is to give the residents of Manchester the opportunity to 
address the board.  All people wishing to speak will have up to three (3) minutes to do so, and 
any comments must be directed to the chair.  Any resident wishing to speak will come forward 
to the nearest microphone, clearly state their name and address when recognized and give their 
comments.  
 
Speakers may offer comments on school operations and programs that concern them.  In public 
session, however, the Board shall not hear personal complaints of school personnel or 
complaints against any person connected with the District.  Other channels are provided for 
Board consideration and disposition of legitimate complaints involving  school district 
employees, which should be referred to the Superintendent.  Speakers are requested to refrain 
from providing confidential information during this comment period.  Any comments that are 
given regarding personnel matters, will not be responded to by the Board or Administration 
during the public meeting, as these items should be discussed in non-public session.

a. If there is no one else present wishing to speak, a motion is in order to take all comments 
under advisement and further to receive and file any written documentation presented 
and to table the remaining minutes for public comment to the end of the meeting for 
those that have not already spoken. 
 
7. Response to Public Comment 
 
There was no one present wishing to speak during the public comment section. 
 
8.   PRESENTATIONS 
 
There were no presentations this evening. 
 
9. ACTION AGENDA 
 
a. Nellie Mae Education Foundation Grant – Manchester School of Technology    
House Build Initiative – by Nicole Doherty, Assistant Superintendent 
 
Assistant Superintendent Nicole Doherty presented a request for the Board to accept a $500,000 grant 
from the Nellie Mae Education Foundation to reestablish the House Build Program at the Manchester 
School of Technology (MST).  Ms. Doherty explained that the District had not completed a student-
built house since 2020 and that the grant would provide an opportunity to restore this important hands-
on learning experience.  She noted that the initiative aligns with the District's strategic priorities of 
growing learners, educators, and systems.  Through the program, students enrolled in carpentry, 
electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and landscaping programs will 
work collaboratively to construct a residential home. 
 
Ms. Doherty explained that the program will provide meaningful real-world experience while 
strengthening student engagement, attendance, graduation outcomes, and career readiness. Students 
will also have opportunities to work toward industry-recognized credentials and develop connections to 
apprenticeships and employment opportunities.  She reported that the District has eight previously 
donated building lots available and has developed strong community and industry partnerships to 
support the program.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 4 of 24 
 
Ms. Doherty reviewed the proposed funding arrangement for the first two years of the initiative. Under 
the proposal, the grant would support approximately $160,000 annually in salaries and benefits for 
existing Career and Technical Education (CTE) instructors.  This arrangement would allow the District 
to redirect existing general fund resources toward consultants and contractors necessary to complete 
construction of the home.  She emphasized that the initiative would not require the addition of teaching 
positions. Rather, the District would leverage the grant award and existing resources to restore the 
program. 
 
Ms. Doherty explained that the long-term objective is to sell each completed home and reinvest the 
proceeds into future construction projects, creating a financially sustainable program that can continue 
providing educational opportunities to MST students. 
 
She requested that the Board approve acceptance of the $500,000 grant and the proposed staffing and 
funding arrangements for years one and two, consistent with the grant award. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Chmiel commended Ms. Doherty for spearheading the initiative and coordinating 
the comprehensive team of District personnel, City departments, and community partners involved in 
its development.  Dr. Chmiel noted that restoring the House Build Program had been a longstanding 
District goal and that obtaining the funding necessary to restart the initiative represented a significant 
accomplishment. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Parr, duly seconded by Committee Member Spencer, it was moved 
to approve acceptance of the $500,000 Nellie Mae Education Foundation grant and the proposed 
staffing and funding arrangements for years one and two of the Manchester School of Technology 
House Build Initiative. 
 
Committee Member Want expressed strong support for the initiative, noting that it would provide 
students with valuable real-world experience while also contributing to housing opportunities in the 
community.  She suggested that the District prepare a meaningful letter of appreciation to the Nellie 
Mae Education Foundation and recommended involving participating students in crafting the 
acknowledgment.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 5 of 24 
 
 
Dr. Chmiel agreed that the Foundation should be recognized and explained that the District planned to 
provide ongoing communication highlighting the work as it progresses.  She suggested that 
Communications staff, including Anna Sabato, work with the program to showcase student 
involvement, construction milestones, and the impact of the initiative throughout the project rather than 
limiting the District's appreciation to a single acknowledgment. 
 
Committee Member Want reiterated her support for involving students in those communications. 
 
Vice Chair O'Connell read a statement submitted by absent Committee Member Cindy Stewart into the 
record.  In her statement, Committee Member Stewart expressed her appreciation for the opportunity to 
serve on the House Build Community Design Team and celebrated the prestigious grant award from the 
Nellie Mae Education Foundation.  She thanked Assistant Superintendent Doherty for bringing together 
a diverse group of community stakeholders and for developing a compelling grant proposal. She 
emphasized that the initiative would provide substantial benefits to students and the Manchester 
community and encouraged her Board colleagues to support acceptance of the grant. 
 
Vice Chair O'Connell expressed agreement with Committee Member Stewart's comments and praised 
those involved in restoring the House Build Program.  He recalled that the program had previously 
operated as a self-sustaining initiative and explained that the sale of completed homes would provide 
funding for subsequent construction projects.  Reestablishing the program would restore an important 
educational opportunity that had been unavailable since 2020. 
 
All were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
 
b. Certification of the Results of Question 2 – by Board Clerk, Angela Carey, and   
District Attorney, Matt Upton 
 
Board Clerk Angela Carey and District Attorney Matthew Upton presented the certification of the 
results of Question 2 from the November 3, 2026, election.  Attorney Upton stated that Question 2, 
associated with House Bill 1300, had appeared on the ballot during the November 3 election.

a. License Agreement with Manchester-Boston Regional Airport (MHT) – by  
Dr. Kelly Espinola, Assistant Superintendent 
 
Dr. Kelly Espinola presented a request for Board approval of a license agreement with Manchester-
Boston Regional Airport to relocate the District's school bus transportation operations back to 
Manchester.  She explained that identifying a suitable long-term location for the District's bus fleet had 
been a significant priority.  When the District initially explored opportunities at the airport in June 
2025, Lot F was unavailable. However, recent changes in circumstances at the airport resulted in the 
space becoming available.  She explained that the proposed relocation would occur in two phases. 
 
1. Phase One — Initial Relocation 
 
Phase One would provide approximately 61,000 square feet of space at Lot F.  During this phase, only 
buses currently in service would be relocated to the airport. Buses that are not actively being used 
would remain at the District's existing location in Candia until additional space becomes available. 
Pending Board approval, the District anticipated relocating its active buses to the airport by November 
24, 2026. 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that the administration was working through the logistics of the transition, 
including bus parking configurations, employee parking, dispatch operations, and other infrastructure 
needs.  She noted that the District was also coordinating closely with First Student to ensure 
transportation services continued without interruption.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 7 of 24 
 
2. Phase Two — Long-Term Transportation Operations 
 
Phase Two, anticipated for April 2027, would expand the available space to approximately 122,000 
square feet.  The additional space would allow the District to accommodate its full bus fleet and better 
support the daily operations of the Transportation Department.  Dr. Espinola explained that Phase Two 
would also include consideration of a proposed ten-year agreement, with options for additional five-
year extensions.  She emphasized that the agreement could provide the District with a stable, long-term 
location for transportation operations. 
 
3. Partnership with the Airport 
 
Dr. Espinola described the proposed agreement as beneficial to both the Manchester School District 
and Manchester-Boston Regional Airport.  In addition to returning the District's buses to Manchester, 
the partnership could provide opportunities for the District to assist the airport with emergency 
preparedness exercises, evacuation training, and other coordinated transportation needs.  She explained 
that this collaboration would strengthen the organizations' shared commitment to public safety, 
emergency preparedness, and service to the Manchester community. 
 
Dr. Espinola thanked airport officials and the District personnel who had worked to identify and secure 
the opportunity. 
 
She requested Board approval of the license agreement for the initial phase of Lot F, allowing the 
District to proceed with the relocation while continuing to negotiate a longer-term arrangement. 
 
Dr. Chmiel expressed appreciation to Dr. Espinola, Attorney Upton, and the District's financial staff for 
their work in developing the agreement.  She noted that the administration had committed during the 
summer to exploring opportunities to return transportation operations to Manchester and was pleased 
that a potential solution had been identified sooner than anticipated. 
 
Mayor Ruais also commended the team and provided background regarding the District's search for a 
transportation facility.  He explained that approximately a year earlier, the District had been required to
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 8 of 24 
 
vacate its previous bus storage location.  During the search for an alternative, the administration 
explored numerous possible sites and worked with several entities, including local institutions, 
businesses, and municipal officials. 
 
Dr. Espinola confirmed that the District had extensively explored available options, including vacant 
lots and existing facilities, some of which would have required more than $1 million to accommodate 
the fleet.  Through the procurement process, the District ultimately entered into an arrangement with 
First Student to provide bus storage and maintenance services in Candia. 
 
Mayor Ruais noted that the newly available airport property presented an opportunity to establish a 
more permanent transportation facility within the City. 
 
Questions and comments from the Board included: 
1. Committee Member Want asked how bus maintenance would be handled following the 
relocation to Manchester.   
 
Dr. Espinola explained that First Student would continue to provide maintenance services under the 
agreement approved at the previous Board meeting.  She noted that the storage portion of the proposed 
First Student agreement had been removed because the District anticipated the availability of the airport 
property.  First Student would continue providing daily support, including morning bus pullout 
operations. Buses requiring maintenance or repair work at a shop would be transported to Candia. 
 
2. Vice Chair O'Connell commended Dr. Espinola and the entire team for their work and asked 
where the District's buses would be fueled. 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that fueling was currently provided through the Manchester Transit Authority. 
However, the administration was also exploring whether a mutually beneficial agreement could be 
established with the Department of Public Works that might result in additional financial efficiencies. 
Vice Chair O'Connell also asked whether the snow removal equipment recently approved by the Board 
would be located at the airport or in Candia.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 9 of 24 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that the proposed equipment purchase and related funding reallocation were 
scheduled for consideration by the Board of Mayor and Aldermen on November 17, 2026. 
 
Following approval, the District would work with First Student or the selected vendor to arrange for the 
equipment to be delivered to the airport.  She emphasized that the intention was to avoid moving the 
equipment more than once. 
 
3. Committee Member Hamer thanked the transportation team for addressing concerns that had 
been raised regarding the buses being located in Candia.  He commended the administration for 
identifying a favorable agreement and moving quickly to return the fleet to Manchester. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Hamer, duly seconded by Committee Member St. John, it was 
moved to approve the proposed license agreement with Manchester-Boston Regional Airport for the 
initial phase of Lot F.  All were in favor and the motion passed.

COMMUNICATIONS 
 
11. Superintendent’s Communications.  
 
a) Superintendent Updates: 
 
Dr. Chmiel informed the Board that a written memorandum containing the administration's updates had 
been provided to members.  She indicated that an electronic copy had also been forwarded to the Board 
Clerk for inclusion on the District's website and in the records of the meeting.   
 
Project Graduation — Saturday Credit Recovery Program 
 
Assistant Superintendent Nicole Doherty provided an update regarding Project Graduation, a Saturday 
credit recovery program designed to support high school students who need to recover academic credits 
and remain on track for graduation.  Ms. Doherty explained that the program provides students with 
direct academic support from Manchester School District teachers, including individualized assistance 
and opportunities to develop plans for successfully completing graduation requirements.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 11 of 24 
 
Sessions are held on Saturdays from 8:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. at Central, Memorial, and West High 
Schools.  A program flyer outlining participation opportunities and additional information was 
provided to the Board. 
 
Ms. Doherty emphasized that Project Graduation represents an important component of the District's 
ongoing efforts to increase graduation rates and provide additional academic pathways for students who 
may be at risk of falling behind. 
 
State Accountability Data 
 
Ms. Doherty informed the Board that the New Hampshire Department of Education was scheduled to 
present statewide accountability results to the State Board of Education on November 12, 2026. 
Following that presentation, the information would be released publicly.  She indicated that the 
administration would provide a more comprehensive review of Manchester's 2026 accountability data 
at the next Board meeting.  The presentation would include information regarding graduation rates, 
College and Career Readiness results, and any District schools identified for Comprehensive Support 
and Improvement (CSI), Targeted Support and Improvement (TSI), or Additional Targeted Support and 
Improvement (ATSI). 
 
Athletics — Fall Sports and Turkey Bowl 
 
Dr. Kelly Espinola congratulated Manchester's student-athletes and coaches on a successful fall athletic 
season. She reported that cheerleading teams from all three Manchester high schools had competed in 
the state championships over the previous weekend. She also highlighted that all three Manchester high 
school football teams had qualified for the postseason, marking a significant accomplishment for 
District athletics.  Although the teams' playoff runs had concluded, Dr. Espinola expressed pride in 
their hard work, dedication, and accomplishments throughout the season. 
 
She then discussed an exciting proposed change to Manchester's annual Thanksgiving football 
tradition, the Turkey Bowl, scheduled for November 26, 2026.  Due to the success of all three 
Manchester football teams and their close power rankings, the coaches developed a proposal to include
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 12 of 24 
 
Central, Memorial, and West High Schools in the event.  Under the proposed format, Memorial High 
School, ranked second, would play Central High School, ranked third, beginning at 10:00 a.m. 
After two quarters of play, there would be a 20-minute halftime featuring the school bands. 
West High School, the highest-ranked team, would then play the winner of the first matchup for two 
quarters.  The winner of the final matchup would be recognized as the City Champion. 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that the format would be implemented as a one-year trial. There would be no 
admission fee, and the overall length of the event was expected to remain consistent with previous 
years.  She noted that West High School would serve as the host school. 
 
Dr. Espinola expressed enthusiasm for the opportunity to include all three high schools in the annual 
tradition and strengthen community participation. 
 
Robotics Update 
 
Dr. Espinola reported on a successful weekend for Manchester's robotics teams, which participated in 
two competitions in Alton, New Hampshire.  On Saturday, Team 501 Power Knights and Team 131 
CHAOS participated in the Battle of the Bay competition.  Team 131 CHAOS finished as a finalist. 
Three students from Team 238 Crusaders volunteered throughout the competition weekend and 
received the Gracious Professionalism Award in recognition of their dedication and support, despite 
their team not competing. 
 
On Sunday, teams participated in Girls Behind the Glass, a competition designed to celebrate and 
encourage women in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).  The event featured 
all-girl robot drive teams and women serving in leadership roles throughout the competition. 
Dr. Espinola reported that Team 501 Power Knights won the competition, while Team 131 CHAOS 
served as an alliance captain. 
 
She congratulated the participating students, coaches, and mentors on their achievements and noted that 
the weekend marked the conclusion of the robotics offseason.  The District looks forward to the 
beginning of the next robotics season in January.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 13 of 24 
 
Human Resources and Staffing Update 
 
Ms. Evans provided an update regarding District staffing and recruitment efforts. 
She reported that the District had recently hired one bus driver, two crossing guards, and two special 
education teachers.  The special education positions included one teacher at Northwest Elementary 
School and one life skills special education teacher at West High School.  Ms. Evans indicated that 
recruitment efforts continue to focus on high-need positions, particularly special education.  She 
explained that Human Resources is working collaboratively with building administrators to develop 
targeted recruitment strategies, including social media campaigns and other outreach efforts.  She also 
provided an update on employee retention data, noting that District analysts were continuing to process 
current retention metrics and that finalized information was expected to be available in the coming 
weeks. 
 
School Start Times 
 
Dr. Espinola provided an update regarding the work of the School Start Time Committee. She 
explained that the Committee had spent several months reviewing relevant research, transportation 
requirements, athletics, staffing, and the potential impact of schedule changes on students and families. 
The goal of the review was to develop school schedules that better support student health, learning, and 
engagement while remaining operationally and financially responsible. 
 
The Committee developed the following proposed schedules: 
School Level Proposed Start Time  Proposed End Time 
High School 8:15 a.m. 3:32 p.m. 
Middle School 8:25 a.m. 3:20 p.m. 
Elementary School 8:00 a.m. 2:30 p.m. 
 
Dr. Espinola emphasized that the proposed changes would maintain the existing amount of instructional 
time at each grade level. She also indicated that changes to school start times could create opportunities 
to improve transportation efficiency and potentially reduce costs.  However, she stressed that the
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 14 of 24 
 
proposed schedules remain subject to ongoing collective bargaining negotiations with the applicable 
bargaining units. 
 
No schedule changes were being presented to the Board for approval at this time, and any 
recommendations would remain contingent upon the outcome of those negotiations.  Dr. Espinola 
thanked the members of the School Start Time Committee for their time, thoughtful discussions, and 
commitment to supporting Manchester students. 
 
Transportation Update 
 
Dr. Espinola reviewed ongoing transportation challenges associated with bus driver staffing shortages, 
particularly those affecting Hillside Middle School.  She reported that Hillside Route One experienced 
delays of approximately 30 minutes on October 28, November 2, and November 5.  Hillside Route Two 
experienced a delay of approximately 15 minutes on November 4.  During those four dates, Hillside 
recorded 55, 68, 38, and 44 student tardies, respectively. 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that although transportation delays had occurred, the school's overall tardiness 
and absenteeism rates on those days remained consistent with typical daily trends, with no unusual 
increases observed.  She reported that Hillside Route One had not had a permanent driver since the 
beginning of the school year, requiring daily staffing adjustments to ensure transportation coverage. 
Dr. Espinola provided an update on driver recruitment and training. One fully CDL-licensed individual 
was awaiting certification, and three additional candidates were entering the second phase of training. 
She acknowledged the inconvenience transportation delays create for students and families and 
reiterated the District's commitment to improving route coverage, reducing delays, and establishing 
more consistent service. 
 
Specialized Transportation 
 
Mr. Roth reported that, as of November 9, 2026, approximately 851 students were actively receiving 
specialized transportation services through the Manchester School District.  He stated that the 
department was coordinating 89 buses and drivers daily, along with 42 monitors, to meet student
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 15 of 24 
 
transportation needs.  Mr. Roth indicated that specialized transportation operations continue to make 
positive progress as the school year advances. 
 
Fiscal Year 2028 Budget Development 
 
Karen DeFrancis provided an update regarding development of the Fiscal Year 2028 budget.  She  
explained that the administration had begun meeting with building principals to review budget needs 
and priorities.  The District anticipated receiving its state adequacy funding estimate by November 15, 
2026.  Information regarding the tax cap was expected to become available in mid-January.  She 
indicated that the administration planned to present the proposed budget to the Finance and Facilities 
Committee and the full Board during February meetings. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Parr expressed support for Project Graduation and asked about the anticipated 
capacity of the Saturday credit recovery program.  Assistant Superintendent Doherty responded that 
the administration anticipated serving approximately 15 to 20 students per high school. 
2. Committee Member Want also expressed strong support for the program, describing it as an 
important and overdue opportunity for students.  She raised concerns regarding how students and 
families would be notified when credit recovery was needed. 
3. Committee Member Want noted that the first academic quarter was nearing completion and that 
students and families would soon receive information regarding grades and credits earned.  She 
emphasized the importance of making families aware not only that a student had failed a course or 
needed to recover credits, but also that the District had established a program to help address the 
situation.  
 
Ms. Doherty explained that Joyce Lewis, Director of Comprehensive Guidance, was working with high 
school principals and school counselors to identify students who could benefit from the program.  She 
also indicated that the administration was coordinating with Anna Sabato to communicate program 
information through social media.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 16 of 24 
 
Dr. Chmiel emphasized that supporting students in meeting graduation requirements is a shared 
responsibility.  She encouraged Board members and others who become aware of students or families 
struggling with graduation requirements to refer them to their school counselors or principals. 
 
4. Committee Member Want agreed but stressed that families may not know what resources are 
available to them.  She recommended implementing a systematic communication process so that 
families receiving notice of a failed course or missing graduation credit would simultaneously 
receive information about recovery opportunities.  She suggested that communications include clear 
instructions, registration information, and potentially a QR code directing families to Project 
Graduation.  Committee Member Want emphasized that families should not have to independently 
discover that the program exists. 
 
Dr. Chmiel agreed and noted that the District should use multiple communication methods to reach 
families.  She acknowledged that students may be reluctant to share information about unsuccessful 
academic performance and that the administration should not rely exclusively on students bringing 
paperwork home.  She indicated that the District would work to strengthen communications with 
families and ensure that information about credit recovery opportunities is shared through appropriate 
channels. 
 
5. Committee Member Want suggested using the District's existing family communication 
platforms to distribute the information. 
 
Dr. Chmiel reiterated the administration's commitment to helping students graduate on time or as 
close to their anticipated graduation date as possible. 
 
6. Student Member Muhammad expressed support for Project Graduation and asked whether the 
Saturday schedule could conflict with Saturday detention requirements. 
 
Dr. Chmiel explained that situations would be addressed individually but emphasized that Project 
Graduation would take priority when a scheduling conflict occurred.  She stated that keeping students
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 17 of 24 
 
on track for graduation is the primary objective and that other arrangements could be considered to 
address disciplinary obligations. 
 
7. Student Member Muhammad also asked whether alternatives were available for students who 
could not participate in Saturday sessions. 
 
Ms. Doherty explained that the District already offers other opportunities through My Turn and 
additional community partners. She encouraged students to work with their school counselors to 
identify credit recovery or academic support opportunities available during the school day. 
 
8. Committee Member Parr asked whether the Board would receive a more comprehensive 
presentation regarding the proposed school start times, including details about how potential 
transportation savings would be achieved. 
 
Dr. Espinola confirmed that a more detailed presentation would be provided but indicated that a 
specific date had not yet been determined. 
 
9. Student Member Muhammad raised questions regarding the different scheduling formats used 
at Manchester's three high schools. She noted that West High School uses a different block 
scheduling structure than Central and Memorial High Schools and asked how the proposed 
changes would affect those schedules. 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that the proposed changes would shift the starting and ending times of each 
school's existing bell schedule.  She emphasized that the proposal would not add or remove 
instructional minutes. 
 
10. Committee Member Georges asked whether a survey related to the proposed start times had 
been distributed.
November 9, 2026, Board of School Committee 
Page 18 of 24 
 
Dr. Espinola responded that it had not. She explained that the School Start Time Committee had 
developed the recommendations and that the information was being presented to the Board as an update 
rather than as a proposal requiring action. 
 
11. Vice Chair O'Connell expressed support for the proposed three-team Turkey Bowl format but 
raised concerns regarding the possibility of moving the traditional Thanksgiving game away 
from Gill Stadium.  He noted the longstanding importance of Gill Stadium to Manchester's 
Thanksgiving football tradition and referenced the community activities associated with the 
event. 
 
Dr. Espinola clarified that although West High School would serve as the host school, she believed the
